title: Largest Subarray Length K
statement:
`nums` is an array of distinct integers and `k` is a length. Among all contiguous blocks of `nums` with exactly `k` elements, return the largest one as an array.

Two arrays of the same length are compared at the first index where they hold different values: the one with the bigger value there is the larger array.
constraints: All values in nums are distinct
notes:
## Intuition

Comparing every window of length `k` element by element works but costs O(n·k). The comparison, though, is decided at the very first position whenever the first elements differ, and since all values are distinct, two different windows always start with different values. So the largest window is simply the one whose first element is largest. The only catch is that a window must fit: its start can be at most `nums.length - k`.

## Approach

1. Compute `lastStart = nums.length - k`, the last index where a window of length `k` can begin.
2. Keep `start`, the best starting index so far, beginning at `0`.
3. For each `i` from `1` to `lastStart`, if `nums[i]` beats `nums[start]`, set `start = i`.
4. Return `nums.slice(start, start + k)`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 4, 5, 2, 3]`, `k = 3`, so `lastStart = 2`. `start = 0` (value `1`). At `i = 1` the value `4` beats `1`, so `start = 1`; at `i = 2` the value `5` beats `4`, so `start = 2`. The answer is `nums.slice(2, 5) = [5, 2, 3]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over the possible starts plus copying `k` values.
- Space: O(k) for the returned array (O(1) extra otherwise).

## Pitfalls

- Do not take the overall maximum: with `[1, 2, 9, 3]` and `k = 3`, `9` cannot start a window of length 3, so the answer is `[2, 9, 3]`.
- The loop bound is `i <= lastStart` (inclusive); stopping one early misses the last window.
- The shortcut relies on distinct values; with repeats, ties on the first element would need a full comparison.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `lastStart` | last index where a length-`k` window fits |
| `start` | start of the best window found so far |
| `i` | candidate starting index |

narration.2: A window of length k can start no later than this index.
narration.3: Assume the window at index 0 is the best until a better start appears.
narration.4: Try every other start where a full window still fits.
narration.5: Distinct values mean the first element alone decides which window is larger.
narration.6: This start has a bigger first value, so its window wins.
narration.9: Copy the k values starting at the best start and return them.
